content.comment_body: I'm looking for a way to run [product_name] on a Mac. Previously, I used [product_name] [version_no], but I only have the installation CD and no CD drive anymore. One of my computers uses OS10.15 Catalina, while another runs OS14 Somora. On the first computer, [product_name] [version_no] is installed, but no longer works because it isn't compatible with Catalina. I attempted to update using the available update package, but couldn't get it working. I don't mind purchasing [product_name] [version_no], but I'm unsure how to install it. I tried using the demo version with hopes of upgrading to a full license, but couldn't get it to start (I did update my Java). I'm uncertain how to proceed. Is there a reliable way to download and pay for a compatible version for an Intel Mac with OS14? Appreciate any assistance, [user_name]
Please use the Support Request option so that [company_name] can provide guidance. Let us know any feedback you receive from [company_name] Support.

To install [product_name] [version_no], you'll need the x86_64 binary of Java Runtime [version_no]. On macOS, you can determine the default Java version by running the java_home command. Note that [product_name] [version_no] uses Java Runtime [version_no] (x86_64) from AWS Corretto.
Hello, I published a separate post detailing the installation process for macOS 15 (Sequoia): [url] Hope this information is useful.

Hi, I read your post, but it didn't help. I purchased an original DVD from [company_name] and am unsure what to do next. Also, the download page you mentioned from [company_name] is no longer available.

analysis.insight_summary: The user faces difficulties installing and using [product_name] on recent MacOS systems, primarily due to software incompatibilities, outdated installation media, unclear download and licensing procedures, and the requirement for specific Java runtime versions. Attempts to resolve issues through demo versions, updates, and legacy software haven't worked, and the download/support system from [company_name] is considered hard to use or insufficient.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expects an easy method to purchase and install a compatible [product_name] version for modern MacOS, including an upgrade from older releases. They seek a straightforward download, installation, and licensing experience with clear guidance and support for their operating system.
